cells.tense: You are here with the pen and the method is holding steady
cells.act: force the change into reality by steady effort
cells.ask: Find the change near you that actually matters and move it one real inch — not the whole plan, just the inch. Then pause and look at what moved.
cells.core:
You have done the work, so you decide from it. The practice holds: you can tell what the next right step is, and you take it, and the fog stops being a place that stops you. The method is yours, built over time, and it carries you even where the whole road is not visible.

What is next is to let the method move something outside your head. A change sits close to you that a stretch of patient effort would shift, and the steady part of you is exactly what it needs. So force one real thing forward by steady effort — slowly, without stopping, until you can point at what moved. Not the breakthrough. The inch. The method is doing what it was made to do; it just wants a hand on material now, not only on the plan of it.
cells.sheetLine: You can see the next step. Take it and move one thing a real inch.
cells.verb: Deciding by method after the work is done
cells.place: In the fog, one step past what you can see

cells.tense: You are bracing for a future you cannot write in, and the method is tightening
cells.act: drop one condition you set and take the step
cells.ask: Name a condition the next step has to meet before you will move — a way it has to go, something that must be true first. Let it fall away, then take the step this week without it.
cells.core:
The method has outrun the situation. In the fog you are demanding a full picture before you move, and when the picture will not come, the demand gets louder instead of quieter. You are trying to write in a future that has not happened, and the trying is spending the energy the step itself needs. The discipline is real; it has turned into a guard on the door rather than a foot through it.

A step is there, waiting behind a condition you set on it — that the timing be right, the plan complete, the answer certain first. Let one of those fall away. Take the step this week without it, and accept that it comes out less finished than you wanted. The fog does not have to clear for you to move through it.
cells.sheetLine: The method is guarding the door instead of walking through it.
cells.verb: Deciding by method after the work is done
cells.place: In the fog, one step past what you can see

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door the method put behind you, and it has gone quiet
cells.act: judge the hurt fairly after it has finished
cells.ask: A matter that is already over, that you keep quietly turning: weigh it once, plainly — what it took from you, what it left. Then put it down, settled.
cells.core:
The method is not in your hands right now. You have come up against uncertainty and stopped arriving at it — the disciplined part of you is still parked at a door that already closed, and it no longer moves you anywhere. You can do the work; you are not bringing it to where you are standing. Ambiguity gets sidestepped instead of navigated, and the fog wins by default.

What charges that back up is not more effort in the fog. It is a fair call made about something finished. One matter keeps getting turned over without ever being settled. Weigh it once, honestly — what it took and what it left, no more and no less. Then put it down. That is where the current comes back from, and it does not ask you to feel anything first.
cells.sheetLine: You have been standing still at a door that already closed.
cells.verb: Deciding by method after the work is done
cells.place: In the fog, one step past what you can see

cells.tense: The pen is down, but you are still reading the road without knowing it
cells.act: sense what has not happened yet, with wonder
cells.ask: Set the step aside and picture where this might be going — not the plan, just the picture. Notice what rises as you do, and give the feeling one word.
cells.core:
You are steering in the fog and calling it analysis. The method is doing the navigating, but so is something else — a quiet sense of where this is going that you do not count as yours. When it shows up, you name it a hunch, or a feeling, or nothing at all. Something in you is reading the road ahead, and it is not on the record as anything you did.

Underneath the method is something older and simpler: the ability to picture what has not happened yet. It does not need your discipline to work. It needs you to notice it. Let yourself imagine where this might go, with no plan attached — not to decide anything, just to see it. What you picture is yours, and it sits there whether or not you claim it.
cells.sheetLine: Something in you is reading the road ahead. It is yours.
cells.verb: Deciding by method after the work is done
cells.place: In the fog, one step past what you can see

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the Too Much cell can describe what the person is bracing against — the record gives only that they are pushing ahead of natural timing in ambiguity, not what future they can't write in. A reader could reasonably say the method is not the problem, their life is; so each cell stays on what the capacity is doing in a moment they could recognize, and none of them explains why. The asks survive being wrong because each is one small act a person can do in a week regardless of whether the read lands, and none promises an outcome. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is the sheet line in Too Little — it is elegant about a starved seat and could make someone feel diagnosed rather than offered, so I have kept it plain and forward-facing instead. Executor at Bridge means the discipline is still forming; Catalyst of Structure's acts are all slow forcing, so the Balanced ask is the smallest real inch of that, not a breakthrough, and none of the four asks can be done for someone else except where the card is about people, which the Too Little medicine allows once and does not require.
